A0235.title: Sim-to-Real Domain Randomization & Consistency Checking
A0235.definition: Narrowing the gap between simulation training and real deployment via domain-randomization training, simulation-reality consistency checking, and real-world red-team testing to prevent attackers from exploiting the reality gap to break policies.
A0235.description: Sim-to-Real domain randomization and consistency verification targets the risk that VLA/RL policies trained in simulation are exploited via the reality gap during real-world deployment, constructing a three-layer defense. First, domain randomization: during simulation training, lighting, textures, and dynamics parameters are randomized to make the policy robust to environmental variations and reduce overfitting to specific simulation conditions. Second, simulation-to-reality consistency verification: after deployment, real observations are continuously compared against simulation predictions, and an alert with degradation is triggered when deviation exceeds a threshold. Third, real-world red-teaming: before deployment, adversarial strategies and perturbations are used in the real environment to test policy robustness and uncover reality-gap attack paths. This measure serves as a core defense following research on Gleave adversarial policies and UPA-RFAS sim-to-real transfer attacks, and complements A0229 (VLA adversarial training and robustness), where the former focuses on model-level adversarial robustness and this measure focuses on sim-to-real transfer robustness.
A0235.limitation: Domain randomization cannot cover all real-world variations, leaving unmodeled physical phenomena; consistency verification relies on accurate simulation predictions, and prediction deviations can be large in complex scenarios; real-world red-teaming is costly and has limited coverage; there is a trade-off between defense effectiveness and policy performance.
